(Fairmont, West Virginia) | college = * [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] (2020–2022) * [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] (2022–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2024 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2024|full=y}} | team1 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team2 = →[[Valley Suns]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team3 = [[Maine Celtics]] | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] (2024) * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team (2021) * [[Bill Evans Award]] (2019) }} '''Jalen Lashaun Bridges''' (born May 14, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]] and the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]]. ==High school career== Bridges played basketball for [[Fairmont Senior High School]] in [[Fairmont, West Virginia]]. He helped his team win back-to-back Class AA state titles in his first two years.{{cite magazine |last1=Welch |first1=Matt |title='All About Basketball': Jalen Bridges' Basketball Career Has Always Been About Learning |url=https://www.si.com/college/westvirginia/basketball/jalen-bridges-basketball-career-has-always-been-about-learning |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 18, 2021 |date=March 19, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Brocato |first1=Joe |title=Fairmont Senior grad Jalen Bridges finds new shooting form, expanded game at WVU |url=https://wvmetronews.com/2020/10/30/fairmont-senior-grad-jalen-bridges-finds-new-shooting-form-expanded-game-at-wvu/ |website=[[West Virginia MetroNews]] |access-date=July 18, 2021 |date=October 30, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 21.6 points, 6.7 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game, leading his team to its fourth straight state title game.{{cite web |last1=Hunter |first1=Greg |title=Jalen Bridges Ready For His Mountaineer Debut |url=https://bluegoldnews.com/west-virginia-mountaineers/jalen-bridges-ready-for-his-mountaineer-debut/ |website=Blue Gold News |access-date=July 18, 2021 |date=November 9, 2020 |archive-date=July 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210719135521/https://bluegoldnews.com/west-virginia-mountaineers/jalen-bridges-ready-for-his-mountaineer-debut/ |url-status=dead }} He won the [[Bill Evans Award]] as the top high school player in the state of West Virginia.{{cite web |last1=Hertzel |first1=Bradley |title=Fairmont Senior's Jalen Bridges wins Evans Award |url=https://www.newsandsentinel.com/sports/local-sports/2019/03/fairmont-seniors-jalen-bridges-wins-evans-award/ |website=[[The Parkersburg News and Sentinel]] |access-date=July 18, 2021 |date=March 24, 2019}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] over offers from [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] and [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web |title=Jalen Bridges commits to WVU basketball |url=https://www.wvgazettemail.com/sports/wvu/jalen-bridges-commits-to-wvu-basketball/article_98076a5a-0f32-5ccc-87dd-7c5820b8974c.html |website=[[Charleston Gazette-Mail]] |access-date=July 18, 2021 |date=September 2, 2019}} ==College career== After initially planning to play a [[postgraduate season]], Bridges joined West Virginia for his first season as a [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]].{{cite web |last1=Hertzel |first1=Bob |title=Fairmont's Jalen Bridges adjusts his game for college play |url=https://www.timeswv.com/news/saturday_news/fairmonts-jalen-bridges-adjusts-his-game-for-college-play/article_c4f8a2ba-1af1-11eb-8182-4ff46073237e.html |website=[[Times West Virginian]] |access-date=July 18, 2021 |date=October 31, 2020}} On March 4, 2021, he recorded freshman season-highs of 22 points and 12 rebounds in a 76–67 win over [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]].{{cite web |title=Jalen Bridges has a career-best game in leading No. 6 West Virginia past TCU |url=https://www.dominionpost.com/2021/03/04/jalen-bridges-has-a-career-best-game-in-leading-no-6-west-virginia-past-tcu/ |website=[[The Dominion Post (Morgantown)|The Dominion Post]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 19, 2021 |date=March 4, 2021}} As a freshman, Bridges averaged 5.9 points and 3.6 rebounds per game, earning [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite magazine |last1=Callihan |first1=Schuyler |title=Jalen Bridges Switches Jersey Number |url=https://www.si.com/college/westvirginia/basketball/jalen-bridges-switches-jersey-number |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 19, 2021 |date=May 19, 2021}} He averaged 8.4 points and 4.8 rebounds per game as a sophomore. Following the 2021-22 season, Bridges transferred to [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]].{{cite news |last1=Watkins |first1=Tim |title=BREAKING: WVU Transfer Jalen Bridges commits to Baylor |url=https://247sports.com/college/baylor/Article/Transfer-portal-Jalen-Bridges-West-Virginia-basketball-commits-to-Baylor-Bears-186480171/ |access-date=November 6, 2022 |work=247 Sports |date=April 20, 2022}} He averaged 10.3 points and 5.6 rebounds per game as a junior. Bridges declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] before withdrawing to return to Baylor.{{cite news |last1=Peery |first1=Wade |title=Baylor small forward Jalen Bridges will withdraw his name from the 2023 NBA Draft |url=https://www.on3.com/pro/news/baylor-small-forward-jalen-bridges-will-withdraw-his-name-from-the-2023-nba-draft/ |access-date=March 9, 2024 |work=On3.com |date=May 31, 2023}} He averaged 12.2 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 1.1 blocks per game and was named to the Third Team All-Big 12.{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Projected second-round pick Jalen Bridges 'forever grateful' to enter NBA draft |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/projected-second-round-pick-jalen-171258695.html |access-date=July 14, 2024 |work=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=June 1, 2024}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Bridges signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]] on July 4, 2024.{{cite web|title=SUNS SIGN JALEN BRIDGES TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-jalen-bridges-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}} Bridges appeared in eight games for the Suns as a rookie, averaging 1.1 points per game. During the [[2025 NBA Summer League]], Bridges played for the [[Boston Celtics]]. He was waived by Boston as part of final roster cuts on October 16, 2025.{{cite web | last=Quinn | first=Justin | title=Report: Celtics cut Jalen Bridges, Kendall Brown, and Wendell Moore | website=Celtics Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2025-10-17 | url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/celtics/2025/10/17/report-celtics-cut-jalen-bridges-kendall-brown-and-wendell-moore/86747646007/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} He joined the Celtics' [[NBA G League]] affiliates, the [[Maine Celtics]], for the 2025–26 season.{{Cite web |title=Maine Celtics Announce Opening Night Roster |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/roster-announced-110625
